children: By Emily Ou Yong
Iron ore futures fell for a fifth session on Tuesday, weighed down by rising shipments, while elevated coke prices squeezed steel mill margins and clouded the demand outlook.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
was 0.56% lower at 707.5 yuan ($105.40) a metric ton.
The benchmark October iron ore (SZZFV6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.3% lower at $95.3 a ton.
Global iron ore shipments rose 1.59 million tons week-on-week to 35.17 million tons in the week to September 13, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.
Coke prices remain high, with some mills entering maintenance amid tight supply, hitting rigid demand for iron ore, analysts from Shanghai Metals Market said in a note.
With demand contracting and supply holding steady, ore prices are likely to stay weak in the near term, the analysts said.
China's daily crude steel output in August fell 3% from the month before to an eight-month low, as some steelmakers scaled down operations amid plunging margins.
China's new home prices also fell again in August, underscoring persistent weakness in the housing market and suggesting the economy will struggle to generate momentum from domestic demand.

Steel mills may have some appetite to restock iron ore ahead of holidays at the end of the month, though the sharp drop in profit margins is likely to keep that restocking drive limited, analysts from broker Chaos Ternary Futures said in a note.
Elsewhere, Indonesia has launched an anti-dumping investigation into imports of galvanised steel products from China, the Trade Ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.
Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE were weaker, with coking coal
NYMEX:ACT1!
little changed and coke (DCJcv1) down 0.27%.
Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were broadly stronger. Rebar
rose 0.42% and stainless steel
edged 0.22% higher, while hot-rolled coil
and wire rod (SWRcv1) were little changed.
($1 = 6.7127 Chinese yuan)
